findings.issue_text: [BUG] The cleanup query deletes reminders with retryCount > 1, but the retry path increments retryCount from 0 by exactly 1 per failure, so a reminder that fails once is never cleaned up and fails again on the next cron run. A reminder that errors on run 1 (retryCount becomes 1) is re-selected by the upcoming-reminders query and re-attempted; the deletion branch only fires after the second failure, so the intended one-retry cap is actually a two-failure cap and every failure path executes one extra full Twilio call + DB cycle before the record is purged. Conversely, reminders with retryCount > 1 but scheduledDate in the future that were never SMS-failed via this path would also be deleted, since the OR branch matches regardless of scheduledDate.

[ADVISORY] The catch block increments retryCount using the stale value read at query time (reminder.retryCount + 1), not an atomic increment. If this handler runs concurrently (overlapping cron invocations or multi-instance deployment), two runs both read retryCount=0 and both write 1, deferring actual cleanup by an additional cycle; also the catch branch double-counts when the error occurs after a successful schedule in the same loop iteration is impossible here, but any parallelism silently mis-tracks retries for operators inspecting the column.

[BUG] The deleteMany OR branch drops the method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter entirely, so ANY WorkflowReminder row with retryCount > 1 is deleted, regardless of method or scheduledDate. Any reminder (email, calendar, SMS) whose retryCount has been incremented past 1 is hard-deleted on the next scheduler run, including rows with future scheduledDates that were never delivered — silent data loss of pending reminders. The sibling-filter SMS scoping that previously constrained the delete is silently lost for the retryCount branch.

[BUG] The else and catch branches increment retryCount from the stale reminder.retryCount value read in the initial findMany, and a reminder that eventually succeeds never has retryCount reset, so a transient failure early in a reminder's life permanently counts toward its retry budget. A reminder that fails once (retryCount=1), succeeds and is rescheduled, then hits one more transient failure is deleted by the retryCount > 1 purge on the next run despite only failing twice overall with a success in between; the retry budget is lifetime-cumulative, not consecutive, which no stated requirement covers.

[ADVISORY] The diff introduces a new retry-cap state machine (increment on falsy sid, increment on thrown error, purge at retryCount > 1) plus a schema migration, but contains zero test files — no spec/test path appears anywhere in the diff. A regression in any of the three coupled branches (e.g., the dropped SMS filter, or the catch-path increment racing the purge) would silently delete or infinitely retry user reminders with no failing test; the acceptance criterion 'failed reminders stop after N attempts' is entirely unverified.

[ADVISORY] The retry cap is off-by-one relative to any natural reading: a reminder is retried at retryCount 1 and 2, and deleted when the next run sees retryCount > 1 — so the second retry attempt is scheduled once but the row is purged at the start of that same run before it can be re-attempted. Operators tuning 'retryCount' expectations (e.g., '3 retries') get 1–2 depending on run timing, and the purge deletes rows whose incremented value was written by the immediately-preceding run in the same invocation order — the exact cap boundary is untested and undocumented.

[BUG] The new deleteMany OR-branch removes reminders with retryCount > 1 regardless of scheduledDate, so a reminder whose scheduledDate is still in the future gets hard-deleted once it accumulates two failures, destroying the scheduled reminder row entirely. A transient Twilio failure twice in a row causes the reminder row to be silently deleted even though its scheduledDate has not yet passed; the attendee never receives the reminder and no record of the missed reminder exists for auditing or manual re-send.

[BUG] The retryCount > 1 deletion branch omits the method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, so it applies to WorkflowReminder rows of every method, not just SMS. Any non-SMS reminder row (e.g., EMAIL) that ever reaches retryCount > 1 — via future code that increments retryCount for other channels or direct DB writes — is deleted by an SMS-only cleanup endpoint; today this is latent contamination of the delete predicate, waiting on the first non-SMS writer of retryCount to silently drop email/calendar reminders.

[ADVISORY] Retry-give-up is implemented by silently deleting the reminder on the next scheduler pass (retryCount > 1) with no logging, notification, or state marking on the abandonment path, and the retry counter is only surfaced via console.log on the error path. Operators get no signal when reminders are abandoned after retries exhaust — a reminder that fails twice disappears from the database entirely, making debugging missed SMS reminders impossible because the evidence row is deleted.

[ADVISORY] The entire retryCount lifecycle — increment in the else branch, increment in the catch branch, deletion at retryCount > 1 — is behavior-bearing new logic with no test anywhere in this diff. A regression in the increment or threshold (e.g., off-by-one turning one retry into immediate deletion, or the deletion branch never firing and infinite retries) would ship unnoticed; the retry cap is the core deliverable of this PR and is unverified.

[ADVISORY] The else branch increments retryCount for reminders that were simply skipped (not sent and not errored), conflating 'scheduler decided not to schedule' with 'send failed', and successful scheduling never resets retryCount on the reminder row. A reminder that enters the else branch for benign reasons burns its retry budget toward the silent delete, and a reminder that succeeded after one failure retains retryCount = 1 forever — one more later benign else/catch hit puts it in the deletion crosshair.

[BUG] The retryCount>1 delete clause has no method filter, so it deletes WorkflowReminder rows of every method (email, SMS, etc.), not just SMS reminders. WorkflowReminder is a shared table across reminder methods; the OR branch { retryCount: { gt: 1 } } matches any row with retryCount > 1. Today only this SMS path increments retryCount, but the schema change makes retryCount a general column on WorkflowReminder, so any future (or parallel) method that uses it — e.g. an email retry implementation touching the same model — has its reminders silently hard-deleted by the SMS cron. The original code carefully scoped deletion to method: WorkflowMethods.SMS; the new branch drops that invariant.

[BUG] Failed reminders are permanently deleted at the start of the next run (retryCount > 1) instead of being marked as terminally failed, silently discarding them with no record, notification, or distinguishing of cause. A booking's reminder that fails twice (e.g. Twilio outage window) is deleteMany'd wholesale on the next cron invocation; the attendee simply never receives their appointment reminder and no row remains to audit or alert on. The delete also destroys the row's other fields (bookingUid, scheduledDate) rather than setting a terminal state, so operators cannot distinguish 'reminder sent' from 'reminder dropped after retries' — a semantic-correctness failure where the retry cap is implemented as data deletion.

[BUG] retryCount is updated via read-modify-write from the stale in-memory reminder.retryCount instead of an atomic Prisma increment ({ retryCount: { increment: 1 } }), so concurrent handler invocations lose updates. The value used (reminder.retryCount) comes from the findMany at the top of the run. Two overlapping cron runs (this is a timestamped scheduled endpoint with no locking) both fetch retryCount=0, both fail, both write retryCount=1 — one increment is lost, so a reminder that actually failed twice is only retried a third time before being deleted, and conversely the deletion threshold is reached off a wrong count. The fix is mechanical: data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }.

[BUG] The catch block increments retryCount even when the error is thrown after Twilio has already accepted and scheduled the SMS, causing duplicate SMS sends on retry. The try block spans the Twilio schedule call and the subsequent reminder bookkeeping. If the Twilio call succeeds but any later statement in the try (e.g. the create/update of the reminder record with referenceId) throws, the catch increments retryCount, the reminder is never marked as scheduled (no referenceId row tying it to the sid), and the next cron run re-invokes Twilio — the attendee gets the same reminder SMS twice or three times. The retry counter conflates 'send failed' with 'bookkeeping after send failed'.

[ADVISORY] The retry limit (delete when retryCount > 1) is hardcoded as a magic literal in a deletion predicate with no named constant, and the max-retry value lives only in this comparison. Anyone tuning retry policy must find a '> 1' buried inside a deleteMany OR clause; a change to the retry cap requires also reasoning about whether the fetch/scheduling loop and any future monitor agree. A named constant (MAX_SMS_REMINDER_RETRIES) next to the increment site would make the two ends of the policy one concept. Consequence is drift risk on the next change, not present incorrect behavior.

[ADVISORY] The retryCount>1 deletion is unbounded by scheduledDate, deleting rows from any time period including the deep past, on every cron tick. Unlike the scheduledDate branch, the retryCount branch scans/deletes across all history each run. With no upper bound it also deletes old failed rows that the scheduledDate branch would have caught anyway, meaning two deletion predicates in the same deleteMany overlap semantically and the reason a given row vanished (past-date vs retry-cap) is unauditable. Operationally: an admin investigating why a reminder disappeared cannot tell which clause removed it.

[BUG] The new deleteMany OR-branch deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of scheduledDate, so the endpoint now permanently drops reminders after two failed attempts instead of just clearing past-date SMS reminders. A reminder that fails twice (e.g., a transient Twilio outage or an invalid phone number) is deleted from the database with scheduledDate still in the future, so the attendee never receives the reminder and there is no record that it was ever attempted — the stated intent of 'retry count tracking' silently became 'delete after 2 tries', a data-loss behavior change with no human-accepted spec for it.

[BUG] The retryCount > 1 delete clause carries no method filter, so it deletes non-SMS reminders too, while every retryCount increment in this diff is SMS-specific. Any Email or other-method WorkflowReminder that ever has retryCount > 1 (e.g., set by a future writer of the shared column, or backfilled data) is silently deleted by the SMS cron, expanding the change's blast radius beyond the SMS retry intent.

[ADVISORY] The else branch increments retryCount when a Twilio create call returns without a sid, treating a successful API response with no message as a failure to be counted toward permanent deletion. A Twilio response that succeeds but omits sid (e.g., queued-from-cache edge responses) causes a healthy reminder to count toward the retryCount > 1 deletion threshold in the same handler's deleteMany, so the reminder is destroyed without any error being logged or surfaced.

[ADVISORY] The catch block increments retryCount on any thrown error, including infrastructural ones like Prisma/network failures, and the deletion threshold is just 2 — so two consecutive cron runs during a platform outage purge all in-flight SMS reminders. Operators experiencing a transient outage of ~2 cron intervals lose every pending SMS reminder permanently (deleteMany with retryCount gt 1), turning a recoverable outage into silent data loss that no alert or log line (beyond a console.log) explains.

[ADVISORY] The deleteMany OR clause drops the method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter for the retryCount > 1 branch, so the bulk delete now matches WorkflowReminder rows of any method (email, SMS, etc.) purely on retryCount, and also drops the scheduledDate-lte guard for that branch. Any future code path (or a backfill/manual update) that sets retryCount above 1 on non-SMS reminders will cause this handler to silently hard-delete those reminders, permanently cancelling customer-facing notifications of other channels; the delete also now fires on retryCount alone regardless of whether the scheduled date has passed, so a reminder still within its 7-day scheduling window is destroyed once retries accumulate.

[ADVISORY] The retry-cap path permanently deletes WorkflowReminder rows via deleteMany instead of marking them failed, destroying the audit record of which reminders exhausted their retries. Operators debugging why a booking's SMS reminders never went out find no rows and no failure record; after 2 scheduling failures the reminder (and its bookingUid/workflowStepId linkage) is irrecoverably gone with no backup/export step before the DELETE.

[BUG] The retryCount>1 branch of the OR drops both the method filter and the scheduledDate filter, so any reminder row with retryCount>1 is deleted regardless of method or whether it is already scheduled. Today only the SMS path increments retryCount, so the blast radius is confined to SMS reminders — but any future code path (or a manual data fix) that sets retryCount>1 on a booking reminder of another method, or on a reminder that was successfully scheduled, has those rows hard-deleted with no backup on the next invocation of this endpoint; the guard the method filter provides has been silently abandoned for the new predicate branch.

[BUG] The new deleteMany OR branch deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1, silently dropping work while the endpoint still returns {ok: true} to the caller. A reminder whose SMS scheduling fails twice (retryCount goes 0→1→2) is deleted on the next invocation with no error result, no log, and no user-visible signal — the customer simply never receives the SMS and the API reports success. This is a hard cap of 2 attempts implemented as silent data deletion rather than a terminal failure state.

[BUG] The catch-block prisma.workflowReminder.update can itself throw (P2025 record-not-found) with no surrounding try, turning a handled Twilio failure into an unhandled exception that aborts the remaining loop iterations and returns a 500. If the reminder row is deleted between the initial fetch and the catch (e.g., a concurrent invocation's deleteMany with retryCount > 1, or a booking cancellation deleting reminders), the update inside catch throws, the for-loop over unscheduledReminders exits early, all subsequent reminders in this batch are never scheduled, and the caller gets a 500 instead of the partial-success shape the endpoint otherwise returns.

[BUG] The retryCount>1 deleteMany branch omits the method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, so it deletes reminders of any method whose retryCount exceeds 1. retryCount is a column on the shared WorkflowReminder model, not SMS-specific; any future (or existing) code path that writes retryCount on an EMAIL or other-method reminder causes this endpoint to delete those reminders outright, cancelling reminders it has no business touching. The OR branch needs the same method constraint as the original query.

[ADVISORY] retryCount increment is read-then-write (reminder.retryCount + 1 from the earlier querySnapshot result), not an atomic { increment: 1 }, so overlapping invocations lose increments. Two concurrent handler invocations (overlapping cron runs or a retried request) both read retryCount=0 and both write 1, so the deletion-based retry cap under-counts and failed reminders persist and retry far beyond the intended 2 attempts. Using data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } } removes the race.

goldens.comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

The try block spans the Twilio schedule call and the subsequent reminder bookkeeping. If the Twilio call succeeds but any later statement in the try (e.g. the create/update of the reminder record with referenceId) throws, the catch increments retryCount, the reminder is never marked as scheduled (no referenceId row tying it to the sid), and the next cron run re-invokes Twilio — the attendee gets the same reminder SMS twice or three times. The retry counter conflates 'send failed' with 'bookkeeping after send failed'.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the `try` block encompasses both the Twilio scheduling call (producing `scheduledSMS.sid`) and subsequent DB bookkeeping (`workflowReminder.update/create` setting `referenceId`). The new `catch` unconditionally increments `retryCount` without persisting the Twilio SID. If the Twilio call succeeds but a later Prisma operation in the `try` throws, control goes to `catch`, `retryCount` is incremented, and the reminder is not marked with the `referenceId` from the successful Twilio schedule. That leaves the system with an SMS scheduled at Twilio but no local marker, so a later run can attempt scheduling again, risking duplicate sends.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The retry limit (delete when retryCount > 1) is hardcoded as a magic literal in a deletion predicate with no named constant, and the max-retry value lives only in this comparison. Anyone tuning retry policy must find a '> 1' buried inside a deleteMany OR clause; a change to the retry cap requires also reasoning about whether the fetch/scheduling loop and any future monitor agree. A named constant (MAX_SMS_REMINDER_RETRIES) next to the increment site would make the two ends of the policy one concept. Consequence is drift risk on the next change, not present incorrect behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a retry policy via a hardcoded literal `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` inside the `deleteMany` OR clause, while retry increments happen in two places (`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`). The finding correctly notes that the max-retry cap is only expressed as a magic number in the deletion predicate and not as a named/shared constant near the increment sites, creating maintainability/drift risk rather than an immediately verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The retryCount>1 deletion is unbounded by scheduledDate, deleting rows from any time period including the deep past, on every cron tick. Unlike the scheduledDate branch, the retryCount branch scans/deletes across all history each run. With no upper bound it also deletes old failed rows that the scheduledDate branch would have caught anyway, meaning two deletion predicates in the same deleteMany overlap semantically and the reason a given row vanished (past-date vs retry-cap) is unauditable. Operationally: an admin investigating why a reminder disappeared cannot tell which clause removed it.

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleSMSReminders.ts`, the `deleteMany` filter was changed to `OR: [{ method: SMS, scheduledDate <= now }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]`. The `retryCount > 1` branch has no `method` or `scheduledDate` constraint, so it will delete *any* `WorkflowReminder` record (including non-SMS and future-scheduled ones) once its retryCount exceeds 1, across all historical data, on every run. This is a concrete, diff-verifiable behavior change that can cause unintended data loss.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new deleteMany OR-branch deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of scheduledDate, so the endpoint now permanently drops reminders after two failed attempts instead of just clearing past-date SMS reminders. A reminder that fails twice (e.g., a transient Twilio outage or an invalid phone number) is deleted from the database with scheduledDate still in the future, so the attendee never receives the reminder and there is no record that it was ever attempted — the stated intent of 'retry count tracking' silently became 'delete after 2 tries', a data-loss behavior change with no human-accepted spec for it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the initial cleanup `deleteMany` to `where: { OR: [...] }` and adds a second branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` that is not constrained by `method` or `scheduledDate`. As written, any `WorkflowReminder` with `retryCount > 1` will be deleted, even if its `scheduledDate` is still in the future (and even if it’s not an SMS reminder). Since the same diff increments `retryCount` on scheduling failures, this introduces a real data-loss behavior where reminders can be permanently dropped after two failed attempts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The retryCount > 1 delete clause carries no method filter, so it deletes non-SMS reminders too, while every retryCount increment in this diff is SMS-specific. Any Email or other-method WorkflowReminder that ever has retryCount > 1 (e.g., set by a future writer of the shared column, or backfilled data) is silently deleted by the SMS cron, expanding the change's blast radius beyond the SMS retry intent.

adjudication.rationale: In scheduleSMSReminders.ts, the prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany() where-clause was changed to an OR between (method=SMS AND scheduledDate<=now) and (retryCount>1). The retryCount>1 branch has no method filter, so this SMS scheduler endpoint will delete any WorkflowReminder record (including non-SMS methods) that happens to have retryCount > 1, which is broader than the SMS-specific retryCount increments shown in this diff and can cause unintended data loss.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The else branch increments retryCount when a Twilio create call returns without a sid, treating a successful API response with no message as a failure to be counted toward permanent deletion. A Twilio response that succeeds but omits sid (e.g., queued-from-cache edge responses) causes a healthy reminder to count toward the retryCount > 1 deletion threshold in the same handler's deleteMany, so the reminder is destroyed without any error being logged or surfaced.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does treat a missing `scheduledSMS.sid` as a failure: in the `else` branch it increments `retryCount` without logging or surfacing an error, and the next handler run will delete any reminder with `retryCount > 1` via the new `deleteMany` OR clause. However, the finding’s core premise (Twilio can “succeed” yet omit `sid`) is not verifiable from the diff, and the reminder would not be deleted in the *same* handler invocation because `deleteMany` runs before the increment. This is still a concrete edge-case/observability concern introduced by the change (silent retry/deletion on missing `sid`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The catch block increments retryCount on any thrown error, including infrastructural ones like Prisma/network failures, and the deletion threshold is just 2 — so two consecutive cron runs during a platform outage purge all in-flight SMS reminders. Operators experiencing a transient outage of ~2 cron intervals lose every pending SMS reminder permanently (deleteMany with retryCount gt 1), turning a recoverable outage into silent data loss that no alert or log line (beyond a console.log) explains.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `retryCount` and increments it in both the `else` branch (when `scheduledSMS.sid` is falsy) and in the `catch` block for any thrown error (`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`). At the start of each run it now deletes reminders with `OR: [..., { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]`, i.e., any reminder that has failed twice (0→1→2) will be purged regardless of `method`/`scheduledDate`. This creates a concrete data-loss path: two consecutive failed scheduling attempts (including transient infra/third-party failures surfaced as thrown errors) will cause reminders to be permanently deleted on the next cron run, with only a `console.log` as feedback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The deleteMany OR clause drops the method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter for the retryCount > 1 branch, so the bulk delete now matches WorkflowReminder rows of any method (email, SMS, etc.) purely on retryCount, and also drops the scheduledDate-lte guard for that branch. Any future code path (or a backfill/manual update) that sets retryCount above 1 on non-SMS reminders will cause this handler to silently hard-delete those reminders, permanently cancelling customer-facing notifications of other channels; the delete also now fires on retryCount alone regardless of whether the scheduled date has passed, so a reminder still within its 7-day scheduling window is destroyed once retries accumulate.

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleSMSReminders.ts`, the `deleteMany` filter was changed to `where: { OR: [ { method: SMS, scheduledDate: { lte: now } }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } } ] }`. The second OR branch has neither `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` nor any `scheduledDate` constraint, so it will delete *any* `WorkflowReminder` row with `retryCount > 1`, regardless of channel/method and regardless of whether its scheduled date is in the past. This is a real, diff-verifiable broadening of deletion criteria and can cause unintended hard-deletes/data loss (including reminders still within the 7-day window).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The retry-cap path permanently deletes WorkflowReminder rows via deleteMany instead of marking them failed, destroying the audit record of which reminders exhausted their retries. Operators debugging why a booking's SMS reminders never went out find no rows and no failure record; after 2 scheduling failures the reminder (and its bookingUid/workflowStepId linkage) is irrecoverably gone with no backup/export step before the DELETE.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a deletion path for reminders with `retryCount > 1` in `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany({ where: { OR: [...] } })`, which will permanently remove those rows rather than marking them failed. The rest of the diff only increments `retryCount` on failures and does not add any failure/audit status field, so exhausted-retry reminders will disappear from the DB on subsequent runs. Whether this is a “bug” depends on intended retention/audit requirements, but the finding’s core claim (deletion vs. failure record) is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The retryCount>1 branch of the OR drops both the method filter and the scheduledDate filter, so any reminder row with retryCount>1 is deleted regardless of method or whether it is already scheduled. Today only the SMS path increments retryCount, so the blast radius is confined to SMS reminders — but any future code path (or a manual data fix) that sets retryCount>1 on a booking reminder of another method, or on a reminder that was successfully scheduled, has those rows hard-deleted with no backup on the next invocation of this endpoint; the guard the method filter provides has been silently abandoned for the new predicate branch.

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleSMSReminders.ts`, the `deleteMany` filter was changed to `OR: [{ method: SMS && scheduledDate <= now }, { retryCount > 1 }]`. The second OR branch has no `method` or `scheduledDate` constraint, so *any* `WorkflowReminder` row with `retryCount > 1` will be hard-deleted regardless of method or whether its scheduledDate is in the past. This is directly verifiable from the diff and can cause unintended data loss if non-SMS rows (or already-scheduled rows) ever have `retryCount` incremented/set > 1.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new deleteMany OR branch deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1, silently dropping work while the endpoint still returns {ok: true} to the caller. A reminder whose SMS scheduling fails twice (retryCount goes 0→1→2) is deleted on the next invocation with no error result, no log, and no user-visible signal — the customer simply never receives the SMS and the API reports success. This is a hard cap of 2 attempts implemented as silent data deletion rather than a terminal failure state.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the initial cleanup `deleteMany` to `OR`-delete any `WorkflowReminder` with `retryCount: { gt: 1 }`, regardless of `method` or `scheduledDate` (see new OR branch). The scheduling loop increments `retryCount` on failures (`retryCount + 1` in both the `else` and `catch`), so a reminder that fails twice will reach `retryCount = 2` and then be deleted on the next invocation with no terminal status, error response, or logging at deletion time. This is silent data loss / dropped work introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The catch-block prisma.workflowReminder.update can itself throw (P2025 record-not-found) with no surrounding try, turning a handled Twilio failure into an unhandled exception that aborts the remaining loop iterations and returns a 500. If the reminder row is deleted between the initial fetch and the catch (e.g., a concurrent invocation's deleteMany with retryCount > 1, or a booking cancellation deleting reminders), the update inside catch throws, the for-loop over unscheduledReminders exits early, all subsequent reminders in this batch are never scheduled, and the caller gets a 500 instead of the partial-success shape the endpoint otherwise returns.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds unconditional `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ where: { id: reminder.id }, data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 } })` both in the non-success branch and inside the `catch` block. That update is not wrapped in its own try/catch, so if the reminder row no longer exists (e.g., deleted by the earlier `deleteMany` now also deleting `retryCount > 1`, or other concurrent cleanup), Prisma can throw (record-not-found), which would escape the `catch` and abort the loop/handler, turning an otherwise handled scheduling failure into a 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The retryCount>1 deleteMany branch omits the method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, so it deletes reminders of any method whose retryCount exceeds 1. retryCount is a column on the shared WorkflowReminder model, not SMS-specific; any future (or existing) code path that writes retryCount on an EMAIL or other-method reminder causes this endpoint to delete those reminders outright, cancelling reminders it has no business touching. The OR branch needs the same method constraint as the original query.
matched_golden_ids: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same bug: in the deleteMany OR clause, the retryCount > 1 condition is missing a WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing deletion of non-SMS reminders (Email/other methods) when retryCount exceeds 1. This matches the golden issue’s scope and root cause.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] retryCount increment is read-then-write (reminder.retryCount + 1 from the earlier querySnapshot result), not an atomic { increment: 1 }, so overlapping invocations lose increments. Two concurrent handler invocations (overlapping cron runs or a retried request) both read retryCount=0 and both write 1, so the deletion-based retry cap under-counts and failed reminders persist and retry far beyond the intended 2 attempts. Using data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } } removes the race.

adjudication.rationale: The diff increments `retryCount` via read-then-write using the previously fetched `reminder.retryCount` (`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`) in both the `else` branch and the `catch` block. If two handler invocations process the same reminder concurrently, both can read the same `retryCount` value and both write back the same incremented value, losing an increment. Since the diff also adds deletion logic based on `retryCount` (`retryCount: { gt: 1 }`), under-counting retries can cause reminders to be retried more times than intended. Using Prisma’s atomic `{ increment: 1 }` would avoid this race.
